summary: Representative Trahan has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI, without describing it as a threat of extinction. Representative Trahan has said a handful of AI companies make models that "could actually cause a catastrophe" and has called for "independent auditors at the labs so they can detect a catastrophe".

Representative Auchincloss has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about industry-specific rules for AI, AI companions and social media for children, legal liability for AI and deepfakes.

Representative Clark has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI criticize letting AI companies police themselves despite the technology's "very real threats", and are otherwise about tax cuts for data centers and AI companies.

Representative Moulton has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their posts on AI are about jobs, autonomous weapons, AI-enabled surveillance pricing and holding technology companies accountable as AI moves too fast.

Representative Pressley has acknowledged that AI could threaten human survival. Representative Pressley has said Congress cannot stand by "while AI and billionaires threaten humankind" and that AI company staff are "sounding the alarm about the threat of AI to humankind". Their other AI statements are about civil rights, discrimination and jobs.

Representative Lynch has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI by co-signing a letter, but not in their own words. A letter to the Speaker they co-signed names risks of "agentic misalignment, mass cybersecurity breaches, and development of biological or chemical weapons". Representative Lynch's own statements on AI are about consumer protection, banking and competition with China.
